Subject: Realtime multiplexing validation plan & open asks

Alex — thanks again for the call this morning. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we have a single source of truth. Notes below are pulled from our conversation; tell me if I mischaracterized anything.

Top pain points you called out:
- Visible lag for first streamed characters in the app (users perceive typing latency).
- High connection counts from mobile/web (3k+ concurrent websockets) causing memory / connection pressure on your edge fleet.
- Head-of-line delays when one slow request holds up batched GPU work.

Current stack you described:
- Client: iOS/Android + single-page web app (WebSocket-based streaming).
- Backend: Node.js service that load-balances to an in-house Triton setup for local models; some legacy endpoints go through a multi-tenant inference layer.
- Typical request: ~512 tokens, lots of short interactive prompts (chat).

Success criteria (we agreed to validate these in PoC):
- p95 first-token latency <= 150ms (preferred target you mentioned: 120ms).
- Support for 3k concurrent streaming connections with multiplexing (reduce open sockets by ~4–10x).
- No regression in generation quality vs. your baseline.
- Clear telemetry: token-level latency broken down by model/runtime and per-connection queue time.

Immediate asks from our side (what we need to scope PoC):
1) Sample traffic: replay file or representative sample queries (anonymized) — a small set of 200–500 requests that reflect distribution (short chat vs. long completion).
2) Peak profile: expected RPS at peak / sustained RPS, and expected ramp (burst length in minutes).
3) A contact on infra/ops side to coordinate TLS/WebSocket settings and firewall/VPC details.
4) Any current telemetry you can share (p95 numbers, traces) so we can baseline before the run.

Proposed PoC plan (high level)
- Week 0: handoff + access + traffic handoff.
- Week 1: small-scale validation against a dedicated pool (smoke tests + connection multiplexing experiment).
- Week 2: production-representative replay (capture p95/tail and concurrency behavior) + follow-up readout.

Next steps
- If you can drop the sample payloads and peak profile into the Drive link we discussed, Ben will take the lead on the test harness.
- Proposed kickoff: Monday, 12 Apr 2027 — 10:00 AM PT (we can adjust).

Attachments: redwood-poc-checklist.pdf (PoC checklist), sample test config stub.

Thanks — Marissa

Alex — great context, thanks. A few quick technical notes and clarifications so we can prep the harness: 

1) Multiplexing approach
- We can support two patterns: connection pool (N websocket clients per server) or per-connection multiplexing (many logical streams over a single websocket). For your mobile fleet, per-connection multiplexing usually gives best headroom.

2) TLS / auth
- We support mutual-TLS for private deployments and token-based auth for hosted endpoints. If egress-only NAT is preferred, we can give a short-lived client cert workflow or a token-based fallback. Jamie, if you have a preference we can align.

3) Telemetry we need from you pre-run
- Example traces (you mentioned you can share) — ideally a CSV with: timestamp, request_id, client_id, queue_enter, queue_exit, model_start, model_end. If not possible, raw spans are fine.
- A small set of representative user sessions (no PII).

4) PoC test plan (more detail)
- Day 0: deploy a dedicated Redwood pool with a model variant matching your baseline.
- Day 1: run a 1k-request replay at low concurrency to validate correctness.
- Day 2–3: scale to 250 RPS sustained; capture p50/p95/p99.
- Day 4: run burst patterns (1k RPS for 3–5 minutes) and verify recovery and head-of-line behavior.

5) Success gates
- p95 first-token <= 150ms for 95% of the test windows during sustained runs.
- No connection churn >1% during steady-state.

Ben will own the harness; Karthik will own measurement instrumentation. We'll produce a short runbook and a readout deck at the end of Week 2.

Couple of asks for you before kickoff: attach the sample_payloads.json (you said you would) and share any current sampling rate for traces. Also tell us whether the majority of your streaming clients are mobile or web — that affects TCP keepalive defaults we suggest.
